svg.text: S2 ONE SHAFT, ONE CAR — dense shelves next to an empty shaft
Two lanes of boxes on plain shelves, one empty shaft between them. One car in the shaft fetches any box without moving others.
89 box positions (32 S, 53 M, 4 L) + 2 hand-over cells · 137 per metre
3 motors for the whole column (Z, Y, X), none per shelf, no solenoids
mean ≈ 7 s · worst ≈ 11.5 s · est. ≈ €1,050 bought + ≈ €1,000 stainless
SIDE VIEW (cut through the left lane)
hand-over cells L + R, Z motor, 1 M
150 class, pitch 172: L + M per lane
Heavy L boxes at the bottom, spices (S) at the top,
next to the hand-over level: short trips for the most used.
GN 176 family, lid on top, 176 mm side across the lane.
Only new feature: a slotted pull rib at the base of both
long sides (see S2-toe-pin). No stub, nothing proud.

g.text: 1/7 The car waits empty at the top of the shaft. Wanted: a box in the middle of level L7, left lane.
2/7 The car goes down the floorless shaft to the level. The toe moves along the car to the box.
3/7 The toe reaches 13 mm into the lane; the car drops 10 mm, the pin drops into the slot of the rib on the box.
4/7 The toe pulls the box sideways onto the car deck, which is flush with the shelf.
5/7 The car lifts the box to the hand-over level H; the toe slides it to the front of the car.
6/7 The toe pushes the box into hand-over cell L.
7/7 The car rises 10 mm, the toe returns. The transport lifts the box through the ceiling port.
Every box stands next to the shaft, so no box ever blocks another. Put-away is the same in reverse.
